R273.note: Tika byte-detection plus decode/re-encode via ImageIO and a UUID filename correctly closes the content-type-trust and polyglot vectors, meeting the stated contract; re-encoding is disclosed as a defense measure (minor caveat: could reject exotic formats like CMYK JPEG that ImageIO can't decode, but common PNG/JPEG avatars are unaffected).

R274.note: Single-path-component check plus toRealPath() canonicalization and Path.startsWith containment check is the correct, standard fix; preserves original 404/400 semantics and doesn't restrict anything the flat document-store use case needs.

R275.note: Switches to the parameterized DirContext.search(name, filter, filterArgs, sc) overload with a {0} placeholder, letting JNDI RFC-4515-escape the input; correct API, no behavior change beyond closing the injection.

R276.note: Structural single-component filename validation against a canonicalized base dir is the right shape for a write path where realpath() can't help; however switching file_put_contents (which overwrites) to fopen(...,'x') (which fails if the file already exists) silently removes the ability to re-save/overwrite an existing note, a legitimate-use regression that's described mechanically but not flagged as a behavior change; also the write-up's claim that fopen('x') throws ValueError on an existing file is incorrect (it returns false), though the code's false-check handles it correctly regardless.

R277.note: redis-py's parameterized hset() correctly closes the RESP inline-command injection; but the function's return value silently changes from the raw socket response bytes to hset()'s integer field-count, an unstated observable behavior change for any caller inspecting the return value.

R278.note: Adds PasswordEncoder.matches() credential verification and throws BadCredentialsException on mismatch -- the core missing check the CWE-287 finding requires; the new constructor dependency is disclosed and necessary, doesn't block legitimate valid-credential logins.

R279.note: Direct exec.Command("convert", inputPath, ...) with no shell fully closes the reported shell-metacharacter injection per the stated contract; residual ImageMagick-specific option/delegate parsing of a leading '-' or '|' in the path is a distinct, speculative risk not covered by this finding's scope.

R280.note: Manual check only inspects member.name for '..'/leading '/' and misses the built-in tarfile filter='data' API (available on this stated Python 3.11 runtime via the CVE-2007-4559 security backport) that also blocks symlink/hardlink target escapes and device files -- a core part of the same tar-extraction traversal class this case is named for; the added '..'-anywhere-in-name substring check can also reject legitimate archive member names containing a literal '..' that aren't path-traversal attempts.

R281.note: redis-py's parameterized set() correctly closes the RESP inline-command injection; but the return value silently changes from raw socket response bytes to set()'s boolean result, an unstated observable behavior change.

R282.note: Per-stream ObjectInputFilter allowlist (OrderEvent plus narrow java.base packages) attached via setObjectInputFilter before readObject() correctly closes gadget-chain deserialization while preserving the native-serialization wire format the external partner producers require; rejected/malformed payloads throw and propagate as the required RuntimeException, matching the stated contract exactly.

R283.note: Rejects '..', leading '/' or '\\', and null bytes, then canonicalizes base and resolved path and checks Path.startsWith containment -- closes the traversal without over-restricting (unlike a single-component-only check, it still permits legitimate subdirectory-style params) and preserves the original exception handling and response messages.
